title: Enforce parity between the Rust and Python implementations in CI
description:
Direction (Ryan, 2026-10-17): Python stays a full, independent port of Kanbus. It is never a wrapper over kbs. This task enforces that the two implementations stay identical, mechanically, so the convention is no longer the only guard.

Problem: the dual implementation (66,500 lines Rust, 38,300 lines Python) is kept in lockstep by convention and the convention is failing. Of the last 300 commits, 52 touched implementation code: 30 both sides, 15 Rust-only, 7 Python-only (42 percent one-sided). Rust honours about 25 KANBUS_* environment variables Python does not. The shared Gherkin suite catches behavioural drift but never diffs the two runtimes: exactly one scenario runs both (features/standup/standup_time_windows.feature:167, tagged @python-parity) and Rust excludes it. tools/check_spec_parity.py runs with KANBUS_PARITY_STRICT=0 and today reports 78 steps missing in Rust and 14 in Python with false positives from unparsed cucumber expressions. 41 scenarios starting 'Given a Kanbus project with virtual projects configured' never reach the real CLI: maybe_simulate_virtual_project_command (rust/features/steps/virtual_project_steps.rs:433, 1,404 lines; python mirror :218) fabricates stdout. _promote_quality_signals_to_stderr (python/features/steps/shared.py:70-75) returns stdout as stderr when stderr is empty, so 453 'stderr should contain' steps enforce a different contract than Rust. Rust ignores @skip so five scenarios are spec in Rust and dead in Python. About 450 lines of #[cfg(tarpaulin)] padding in rust/tests/cucumber.rs:201-648 export cover_* functions from the production crate and never compile under llvm-cov.

Work:
1. Parity lane in CI: a fixture script of a few dozen golden commands run against both CLIs (kbs and kanbus), diffing normalised stdout, stderr, exit code and the resulting project directory. Issue files must be byte-identical (the file-fidelity work in kbs-232185 already made the serializers match).
2. Make tools/check_spec_parity.py tag-aware and cucumber-expression-aware, then set KANBUS_PARITY_STRICT=1.
3. Delete the simulated virtual-project CLI and run those scenarios against a real multi-root temp tree in both runtimes.
4. Remove the stdout-to-stderr promotion and fix the scenarios that depended on it; honour @skip in the Rust harness; delete the tarpaulin padding and the cover_* exports.
5. A CI check that fails when rust/src changes without python/src (and vice versa) unless the PR carries a 'parity-exempt' label.
6. Document the KANBUS_* environment variables Python lacks and either port them or list them as intentional Rust-only.

Acceptance: parity lane green on develop; strict spec parity green; no simulated CLI code under features/steps. No decision is needed from Ryan.

comments.text: Handoff status 2026-10-19: Merged so far: PR #428 (parity lane), #429 (strict parity), #430 (honest stderr). CI now has cli-parity, python-console-parity, rust-console-parity and implementation-cochange jobs, and a parity-exempt PR label exists. Not verified: whether KANBUS_PARITY_STRICT is on for every step group, and whether the roughly 25 Rust-only KANBUS_* environment variables are now honoured by Python. Note that implementation-cochange failed on PR #470 (a Rust-only console change that carries the parity-exempt label), so check that the exemption is honoured. Next step: re-run tools/check_spec_parity.py strictly, list what still diverges, and close the task or file the remainder as children.
